validated_mechanisms.mechanism_name: State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval: stepwise skill retrieval scored by fused task-goal + current-state-summary cosine similarity with MMR reranking
validated_mechanisms.source_actor_or_paper: SGDR - 'Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval', arXiv:2606.04391; official code https://github.com/plusnli/online-skill-learning (CC BY-SA 4.0; canonical URL verified live by audit run 32800296360)

validated_mechanisms.reproduction_verdict: REPRODUCED_USEFUL (preregistered combined rule evaluated exactly as frozen)
validated_mechanisms.maximum_defensible_wording: In a preregistered clean-room reproduction on SPIDER's Graph fragment store (12 fragments, 3 sandbox sites, scripted policies, lexical-hash embedder, deterministic summarizer), SGDR-style stepwise retrieval scored by alpha*cos(task, desc) + (1-alpha)*cos(current-state summary, desc) with pool top-M=max(3k,20) and greedy MMR (lambda=0.7) retrieved executable-correct fragments strictly more often than task-text-only retrieval with identical reranking machinery under paraphrased goals and shifted entry contexts (36/74 vs 25/74 correct@1; 11 paired wins, 0 reversals). Auditor-side controls show the gain requires the correct current-state summary: fusing a wrong-context summary or using a summary-only score falls back to baseline level (both 24/74). Under identical execution policies the advantage converted into fewer novel exploration actions than task-only retrieval on both goal regimes (39 vs 42 literal; 36 vs 42 paraphrase) with equal-or-higher subgoal success (.90/.90 vs .90/.80). The retrieval-level advantage is concentrated in one site's dynamic-content menu-disambiguation cluster (int.dyn.nav/ex2/start; 8/2/1 wins); no advantage over task-only retrieval was observed for login/pager addressing. Relative to hand-authored exact goal_sig addressing, the mechanism wins only in the natural-language-consumer regime; when signatures exist, exact addressing remains more action-efficient (21 vs 39 novel on the literal slice). Evidence tier: PROOF OF CONCEPT. Not established: WebArena-scale effects, neural embedders, LLM summarizers, larger libraries, cross-site/cross-domain transfer, robustness of constant-text fusion controls under hashed embeddings.

any claim that login/pager addressing improved
any citation of a constant-dummy-text 24/74 ablation figure as evidence
disclosed_caveats_that_travel_with_the_m: Rule-aggregation ambiguity: under the strictest per-slice reading the conversion rule fails on the literal slice vs incumbent exact addressing (39 vs 21 novel actions); the operational advantage over the incumbent exists exactly and only in the natural-language-consumer regime.
Lexical-hash embedder regime (neural embedder unavailable offline); absolute numbers may differ with real embeddings; effect size not transferable untested.
Deterministic contract-faithful summarizer replaces the reference LLM summarizer.
Small scripted setting: 12 fragments, 3 sandbox sites, tiny n, no uncertainty intervals, correlated queries within subgoals.
Same-site reuse only; cross-site/cross-domain transfer untested here AND by SGDR's authors.
WebArena headline numbers (37.5% GPT-4.1 / 24.3% Qwen3-4B) were NOT reproduced (out of prereg scope).
Insert-time dedup, sliding-window induction, verification prompts not reproduced.

Mechanically-derived descriptions are weak keys for some clusters (books travel/open-first/paginate unsolved at hard@1 for ALL text conditions) - description quality, not fusion, is the binding constraint there.
Fix timing for 4 hash-drifted implementation files remains attestation-based (bounded behaviorally by byte-identical regeneration and independent recomputation).

validated_mechanisms.maximum_defensible_wording: In a preregistered clean-room reproduction on public sandbox targets (scripted policies, no LLM agents), a three-tier capture->extract->parameterize->replay route ladder learned replayable first-party-JSON routes passively during genuine scripted browser task completion on both API-tier tasks (httpbin.org form submission and cookie-state read; discovery 2/2 with output equivalence at discovery time) and completed repeat tasks by direct HTTP replay with zero browser actions at 100% output equivalence, at median wall-clock speedups of 37.05x and 8.66x vs full scripted browser traversal under a realistic network-idle load policy (10/10 interleaved paired wins, 5 measured passes per arm per task, warmups excluded, 0 exclusions). Bare HTTP with perfect public-doc knowledge ran at parity or slightly faster than replay (median C/B ratios 0.92 and 0.73), so NO latency advantage over raw HTTP may be claimed; the demonstrated value of the route abstraction is reaching parity without privileged endpoint knowledge plus parameter-template generalization to unseen records (P1: induced {id} template replayed two newly created bookings field-equal to direct-API ground truth). The no-silent-substitution core held under forced stress: corrupted-auth replay returned structured AUTH_FAIL with no output presented (positive control round-tripped), past-TTL replay refused with STALE_TTL, deleted-record replay surfaced HTTP_ERROR with escalated provenance confirming absence, and the store is structurally pointer-only (no cached response bodies). On server-rendered no-API targets the ladder correctly found zero qualifying routes and escalated to a hand-authored HTML-extraction tier (books.toscrape payload correct; on quotes.toscrape the fallback itself failed in-run with SCHEMA_MISMATCH surfaced honestly - a reliability datum, no substitution occurred). Evidence tier: PROOF OF CONCEPT. Not established: the vendor's 94-domain 950ms-vs-3404ms headline (untested here; remains OFFICIAL_CLAIM with prior forensic qualifications and zero independently confirmable citations as of audit time), any multi-host API-tier result (single-host httpbin slice after a live-verified environment change removed the planned second host's UI), shared-route-graph ranking, schema-drift detection, LLM-agent operation, token costs, or production/anti-bot-walled behavior.

Scripted policies, no LLM agents: token costs structurally zero in all conditions; n=5 measured passes per arm per task.
